messages.subject: Optimization of the pause times
parts:
Hello,

I used the example on GitHub for the parameter optimization(simmer.optim) for the pause breaks that I asked on the other topic, but I'm getting very strange results. Maybe I'm missing some conceptual thing here or my code has some mistake.

The questions is, given a set times for the resources to have a break, what combination would give more finished arrivals (completed events)?
So, for the example, I set that the nurse and cardiologist would be allowed to take a 5min break, every hour. The break could be at 1:20 or 1:25,1:30...1:50 and so on for each hour that I'm simulating. The code is this:

library(simmer)
library(simmer.optim)

sim_model<-function(){
  
  t0<-create_trajectory() %>%
    seize("nurse") %>%
    timeout(function() rpois(1, 10)) %>%
    release("nurse") %>%
    seize("cardiologist") %>%
    timeout(function() rpois(1, 20)) %>%
    release("cardiologist")
    
  pause1<- trajectory("Pause") %>%
    seize("nurse") %>%
    timeout(5) %>%
    release("nurse")
  
  pause2<- trajectory("Pause") %>%
    seize("cardiologist") %>%
    timeout(5) %>%
    release("cardiologist")
  
  env<-simmer() %>%
    add_generator("patient", t0, function() .opt("interarrival_time")) %>%
    add_generator("pause1", pause1, from(.opt("pause1_time"), function() 60),priority=1,mon=0)%>%
    add_generator("pause2", pause2, from(.opt("pause2_time"), function() 60),priority=1,mon=0)%>%
    add_resource("nurse", .opt("nr_nurses"),preemptive=TRUE) %>%
    add_resource("cardiologist", .opt("nr_cardiologists"))
  
  env
}

assert_within_budget<-function(envs, budget){
  runtime_hrs <- (msr_runtime(envs)-40) / 60
  number_nurses <- msr_resource_capacity(envs, "nurse")
  number_cardiologists <- msr_resource_capacity(envs, "cardiologist")
  
  (number_nurses * runtime_hrs * 50 +
      number_cardiologists * runtime_hrs * 100 ) <= budget
}

r<- simmer_optim(
  model = sim_model,
  method = de_optim,
  direction = "max",
  objective = msr_arrivals_finished,
  constraints = list(with_args(assert_within_budget, budget = 1000),
                     with_args(assert_avg_waiting_time_max, max_val = 30)),
  params = list(nr_nurses = par_discrete(1:4),
                nr_cardiologists = par_discrete(1:4),
                interarrival_time = par_discrete(c(10, 15, 20, 25)),
                pause1_time=par_discrete(c(20,25,30,35,40,45,50)), # here the starting times for the breaks
                pause2_time=par_discrete(c(20,25,30,35,40,45,50))
                ),
  control = optim_control(run_args = list(until=4*60),
                          de_optim = RcppDE::DEoptim.control(itermax = 10,trace = T)))
r

The problem is, every time I run the simulation, I get different results for the pause time. 
Does that mean the function has multiple minimums? What am I doing something wrong on the code?

At first glance, I see a couple of problems. First, minor, is that
your cardiologists are not preemptive, so they are not taking their
pause when they are supposed to. Secondly, the pauseX_time variables
just set the starting time for the pauses, so I would say that they
shouldn't impact the results in the long run. In other words, once the
algorithm finds optimals for nr_nurses, nr_cardiologists and
interarrival_time, you are basically searching in a more or less flat
space for pauseX_time.

--

Thanks for clarifying! 
I suspected this could be the problem and I confirmed by doing the substitution of the starting time for the pause one by one. It doesn't change the final result at all. It means that it doesn't matter when you start the pause, it will have the same effect on the result, in terms of completions or service time.
